audience.prompt: Team 3 is free. Where does it go?

a.name: Gemünd South
a.consequence: 1,375 vulnerable people get a team; the power asset stays on the watch list.

b.name: Heimbach Valley
b.consequence: 1,442 people and 2,800,000 EUR of value get a team; the power asset stays on the watch list.

audience.tradeoff: A substation on open road keeps power on. Dense housing keeps people safe. Both are defensible; the room decides.

assessment.title: GeoResponse assessment — Eifel ridge wildfire
assessment.summary: Eifel ridge wildfire affects 34 km². 14 priority sites remain after review; 0 finding(s) were rejected by an analyst. The top three sites (W04, W13, W07) carry €40,400,000 of exposed value and 14,835 people within 700 m. Three response teams are allocated by urgency, access and value at risk.
assessment.headline: The highest-ranked site is Gemünd South (W04), severity red, confidence 75%. A 9,963 m² change intersects debris access; 1,375 people live within 700 m and the insured value is €7,100,000.
limitations: Change extent is derived from a simulated Sentinel-2-like 10 m composite in the demo pack; production uses licensed imagery.
Dark roofs, wet pavement and deep shadow can mimic structural damage; every rejection is retained in the audit trail.
Population is a 700 m radius estimate from the demo population grid, not a household count.
No site is approved automatically. A human analyst signs the assessment before any claim or dispatch decision.
